subject: Quant follow-up: regional routing, latency & data residency requirements
messages:
From: Samir Patel <s.patel@globobank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — perf targets and residency (recap + files)

Vanessa / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — Alyssa and I pulled together the high-level non-functional requirements and attached a small XLS with our estimates. Quick recap of what matters most for us:

- Latency: end-to-end p95 for LLM responses (first token) should be under 120ms for US and EU traffic; APAC is a harder target (we can accept p95 up to 220ms). For streaming scenarios (long responses), we care about stable chunk latency (first chunk p95) and streaming jitter.
- Throughput: baseline expected peak of ~180 req/s (text generation endpoints) across the account, with short spikes to ~350 req/s during market-open bursts.
- Concurrency: we expect up to 40 concurrent model sessions per region, but concurrency-per-instance guidance welcome.
- Streaming: the app streams intermediate tokens; we need support for chunked streaming and a max chunk size of ~64 tokens. Reconnection semantics must preserve KV cache or allow fast warm start.
- Multi-region routing: we will route traffic by user region (US/EU/APAC). EU traffic must be constrained to EU-resident inference and logs. APAC traffic ideally runs in a private VPC due to regulatory constraints in some countries.
- Data residency: EU logs & audit trails must remain in the EU. For APAC we have mixed requirements — some sub-products require full on-prem or VPC-only hosting.

Next steps we asked for on the call: a short written proposal with quant targets we can sign off on, and an internal benchmark plan and a short checklist we can run with our infra. I'm attaching the XLS and a diagram.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the p95 targets in US/EU with a streaming workload and what the recommended instance footprint would be for the throughput/concurrency above? Also — what does the fallback look like if we need to shift to a smaller model during spikes (automated routing / model variants)?

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Senior PM, AI Platform
GloboBank

Attachments: globo_nonfunctional_requirements.xlsx, regional-routing-diagram.png

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <s.patel@globobank.com>, Alyssa Wong <alyssa.w@globobank.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — perf targets and residency (recap + files)

Samir / Alyssa — thanks for the detailed sheet and the clear priorities. Below is a concise proposal and the immediate next steps we recommend so you can validate with infra and compliance.

Quick answers up-front: yes — Redwood can meet the US/EU p95 target for first-token under 120ms in typical gen workloads with streaming, assuming the following configuration per region:
- Recommended model & execution: 34B FP16 / int8 quantized variant (we can provide a smaller 13B fallback).
- Latency buffering: continuous batching enabled with a max batch latency of 8ms and adaptive batching to prioritize low-latency paths for interactive requests.
- Throughput sizing: to meet sustained 180 req/s and spikes to 350 req/s with headroom we recommend a cluster of 4 dedicated inference nodes (r5-class GPUs) per region with autoscale headroom; exact GPU SKU suggestion attached in the bench doc.
- Concurrency guidance: our runtime supports ~32-48 lightweight concurrent sessions per node for 34B quantized models; that maps to your 40 concurrent sessions with the above cluster sizing. If you need hard concurrency guarantees we can pin capacity (Dedicated) per region.
- Streaming behavior: we support chunked streaming and recommend 32–64 token chunk sizes; to preserve KV state on reconnect we use prefix caching + session affinity — we'll share the warm-start checklist.
- Fallback & variants: smart routing rules can fail over to a 13B quantized model variant in the same region automatically; we can also use model-rate-limited fallbacks to degrade gracefully.

Data residency and regional routing notes (important):
- EU traffic: inference and logs can be kept entirely within EU regions (we have EU Dedicated clusters). We can also ship audit logs to your EU S3 bucket or your KMS.
- APAC: we recommend Private deployment in APAC (VPC + customer-managed gateways) for the sub-products that require it. For regions where we operate a hosted APAC region we can route non-sensitive traffic there; sensitive traffic must remain in customer VPC or Private.

Proposed bench plan (we'll run with your test data):
1) You provide 24h representative request logs (sanitized) or a synthetic workload (we accept both).
2) Redwood runs a regional benchmark in US/EU/APAC with streaming enabled (report: p50/p95/p99 first-token and per-chunk latencies, throughput curves, memory/KV hit rates).
3) We provide a regression alert plan (prompt sets + evals) so quality is validated if we auto-fallback to smaller model.

Immediate next steps / asks from GloboBank:
- Share a sanitized 24h+ workload or the XLS + a short sample trace (S3 link or HubSpot doc).
- Confirm which APAC markets need Private VPC vs. hosted.
- Provide a preferred week/time for a 45-minute bench review demo (we suggest Wed 13–15 UTC next week).
- Sign the mutual non-disclosure addendum (I will attach).

I've attached the bench run instructions and a short sizing sketch; looping Aditya and Neha to scope infra and to propose an internal PoC runbook.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192

Team — forwarding GloboBank's requirements and my proposal. Please see the highlighted asks and confirm feasibility:

- Can our EU Dedicated clusters sustain p95 < 120ms for first token on streaming workloads for a 34B quantized model when configured with continuous batching? We need a quick verification that 4 inference nodes per region is reasonable as a starting point.
- Can you outline the expected GPU SKUs (and an estimated monthly cost ballpark) for: (a) Hosted Dedicated per-region cluster, (b) Private VPC in APAC?
- Can we support session-affinity + KV-snapshot warm-start on reconnect as outlined? If not, propose alternatives.

I'll coordinate the bench run once we confirm infra assumptions. Please add notes inline and I will consolidate for Samir.

Thanks — V.

Vanessa / team — good plan, thanks. A few clarifications before we hand to infra: 

- APAC: Singapore and Australia are the main markets. Both will require Private VPC for payments product; other product traffic can land in hosted APAC.
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent sessions is the peak across our web cluster; most sessions are short-lived (user messages < 250 tokens) but we will have periodic long-form generation for reports (~2k tokens).
- Fallback: yes please describe quality guardrails — we need to ensure the 13B fallback only triggers when latency/throughput thresholds are breached and that we have an eval metric that tracks key prompt outputs.

We will: upload 48 hours of anonymized request traces to the S3 link in your bench doc by COB Monday, and we can confirm a Wednesday 14:00 UTC bench-review demo. I'll also sign the NDA addendum — please send.

One more ask: could you provide a small, runnable curl example for streaming that preserves session affinity and shows reconnect semantics so our infra can test quickly? That will speed approvals.

Regards,
Samir
